{"self_assessment": "**Impact:** Our table built a left-facing fish, and when the start domino was pushed, about 109 of the 120 standing dominoes were connected to it. I closed the join in the bottom line near the tail, which carried the fall through to the tail. I also started taking down a stray vertical line that wasn't on the pad. Priya was clearing the same loop, so the two of us overlapped there. I was assigned the tail fin, but Leo had already taken it over, and the fin came out rounded rather than the pointed shape on the pad. I should have either started on it right away or said early that I couldn't take it. The fish should still read as a fish, but the tail is the weakest part of the picture.

**Execution:** My work was careful and I kept it out of other people's lines. I started the takedown below the bottom line so I wouldn't disturb it. I checked the bridge afterwards and then went hands-off, which helped avoid bumps near the end. The tail stroke wasn't traced from the pad, and I didn't speak up soon enough about the doubled-up cleanup.

**Collaboration:** I listened more than I spoke early on. When Maya and I both reached for the same join, I told her I'd keep it and suggested she check the tail instead. I kept my updates short and clear, confirmed the final checks, and left the finishing work to the others once things were settled. I could have reached out sooner when the tail assignment slipped.

**Leadership:** I wasn't the one steering. Leo set direction and Maya and Priya coordinated checks. My contribution was dependable follow-through and staying out of the way when more hands would have caused bumps. Next time I'll speak up earlier when an assignment isn't working, so the table doesn't have to cover for me."}
